claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Local chemical-order fluctuations are relevant structural mediators of mechanical behavior.
Interfacial phase coherence is a relevant mediator of the target mechanical properties in hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Transformer self-attention can capture intricate elemental interactions in high-entropy alloys.
Transformer self-attention can capture the multiscale heterogeneities of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Parameters derived from binary phase diagrams can encode information relevant to HEA phase stability.
Engineered descriptors of atomic or local chemical order can contribute to prediction of mechanical properties.

Combining transformer representations, phase-stability features, and local-order descriptors will learn structure-property relationships more efficiently than exhaustive thermophysical or ab initio calculations.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed model will predict yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed model will predict fracture toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 within ±10% of experiment.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by about 50% relative to conventional CALPHAD and first-principles workflows.
First-principles searches over multicomponent-alloy design spaces have high computational demands.
The model's intended scope is ambient tensile and fracture testing while the intrinsic hierarchical structure is preserved.
The approach assumes that processing history preserves stable local chemical order.
The methodology may become unreliable after processing or extreme thermal treatment significantly disrupts the hierarchical structure or local chemical order.
The methodology may become unreliable for phase behavior outside its calibrated compositional domain.
Transformer models have shown promise for predicting mechanical properties in related high-entropy-alloy datasets.
The exact accuracy and efficiency gains for HfNbTiVAl10 remain unvalidated.
Model performance may be sensitive to feature selection and data quality.
